prompt: Into how many categories does Figure 20.6.1 group the general reactions of carboxylic acids?
explanation: The four categories are deprotonation, reduction to an alcohol, nucleophilic acyl substitution (replacing the –OH) and α substitution.

prompt: In what way do carboxylic acids react like alcohols?

choices.text: They are deprotonated to anions that act as S_N2 nucleophiles
They undergo addition of nucleophiles to the carbonyl group
choices.why: That is how carboxylic acids resemble ketones, not alcohols.

choices.text: They are reduced by LiAlH4 to give primary alcohols
choices.why: Reduction by LiAlH4 is a reaction of the acid's carbonyl group, not something alcohols do.

choices.text: Their –OH is replaced in nucleophilic acyl substitution
choices.why: Nucleophilic acyl substitution is a carbonyl-group mechanism, one of those left for Chapters 21 and 22.

explanation: Like alcohols, carboxylic acids can be deprotonated to give anions, which are good nucleophiles in S_N2 reactions. Like ketones, they undergo addition of nucleophiles to the carbonyl group.

prompt: Which two categories of carboxylic acid reactions does the section call fundamental carbonyl-group mechanisms, to be discussed in Chapters 21 and 22?

choices.text: Nucleophilic acyl substitution and α substitution

choices.why: These were already covered: acidity in Sections 20.2 through 20.4 and LiAlH4 reduction in Section 17.4.
Deprotonation, the acidic behavior of carboxylic acids, was discussed in Sections 20.2 through 20.4.
Reduction by LiAlH4 was already mentioned in Section 17.4.

explanation: Of the four categories, acidic behavior was covered in Sections 20.2 to 20.4 and reduction by LiAlH4 in Section 17.4. The other two, nucleophilic acyl substitution and α substitution, are fundamental carbonyl-group mechanisms discussed in Chapters 21 and 22.

prompt: Which reagent reduces a carboxylic acid to an alcohol, as mentioned in this section?

choices.why: KMnO4 is an oxidizing agent; it makes carboxylic acids from alkylbenzenes and aldehydes.
NaOH deprotonates a carboxylic acid to give its carboxylate salt.
CO2 carboxylates Grignard reagents to make carboxylic acids.

explanation: Reduction by treatment with LiAlH4 (Section 17.4) converts a carboxylic acid into an alcohol. It is one of the four general reaction categories in Figure 20.6.1.

prompt: Which sequence converts benzyl bromide, C6H5CH2Br, into 2-phenylethanol, C6H5CH2CH2OH?

choices.why: The carbon must be added first. Cyanide displacement and hydrolysis give phenylacetic acid, which LiAlH4 then reduces.
That gives phenylacetic acid, C6H5CH2CO2H. A final LiAlH4 reduction is still needed to reach the alcohol.
KMnO4 is an oxidizing agent. Turning the –CO2H into a –CH2OH group needs a reduction with LiAlH4.

explanation: 2-Phenylethanol has one more carbon than benzyl bromide. Cyanide displacement then hydrolysis gives phenylacetic acid, C6H5CH2CO2H, and LiAlH4 reduces the acid to the alcohol C6H5CH2CH2OH (Exercise 20.6.1).
